summary: Story 132.6 records horizontal scaling readiness boundaries only. It classifies service scale safety, singleton authorities, coordination boundaries, ingress/load-balancer readiness, unsupported scaling modes, rollback, and observability without activating live scaling, provisioning hosts, credentials, external load balancers, or production mutations.

default_preservation.required_statement: Local single-host SQLite defaults remain unchanged; all horizontal scaling is deferred until a later activation story supplies operator evidence.

registry-api.reason: HTTP read/write facade can be horizontally scaled only after shared idempotency storage, shared registry-state database, trace propagation, auth preservation, and bounded DB pool composition evidence exist.
registry-api.limit_note: No host ports or external load balancer are added by Story 132.6; rate-limit and idempotency storage must be shared before more than one instance.

registry-state.reason: Mutable registry-state writer/materializer and schema authority must remain single-owner to preserve task/session consistency and ordered event replay.
registry-state.limit_note: Maximum one mutable writer/materializer and one Alembic migration runner; read-side scaling requires a later approved story.

telegram-gateway.reason: Operator ingress remains profile-gated; webhook delivery, auth headers, trace propagation, and rate-limit behavior need explicit load-balancer evidence before scaling.
telegram-gateway.limit_note: No live dashboard or Telegram ingress scaling is activated; sticky sessions are not generally required except Telegram webhook caveats must be evaluated.

orchestrator-adapter.reason: Spawner coordination depends on task/session registry consistency, worktree lock ownership, capability tiers, and shared MCP/idempotency boundaries.
orchestrator-adapter.limit_note: No external worker pool is supported; adapters must not create duplicate runners for a single task/session authority.

worker-wrapper.reason: Worker instances need shared worktree lock ownership, approval/capability tier preservation, and idempotent task/session transitions.
worker-wrapper.limit_note: External worker pools remain unsupported; local/stdin defaults remain unchanged.

clawhip-daemon.reason: Clawhip bridge/event append authority must remain single-owner per event log to prevent duplicate or reordered append streams.
clawhip-daemon.limit_note: Maximum one bridge appender per event log; multi-clawhip appenders are explicitly unsupported.

mutable_registry_state_writer_materializ.reason: One mutable registry-state writer/materializer preserves materialized task/session consistency.

alembic_migration_runner.reason: Exactly one Alembic migration runner prevents concurrent schema mutation.

retention_apply_destructive_lifecycle_ru.reason: Retention/apply/destructive lifecycle actions remain single-runner, approval-bound, and outside live scaling.

event_append_authority.owner: registry-api or clawhip bridge per approved event-log boundary
event_append_authority.reason: One append authority per event log preserves event ordering, replay, and idempotency.

clawhip_bridge_authority.owner: clawhip-daemon or clawhip-bridge-mcp per selected profile
clawhip_bridge_authority.reason: The clawhip bridge authority must be explicit and singleton to avoid duplicate bridge appenders.

coordination_boundaries.reason: All stateless API instances must share idempotency state before duplicate-request replay can be safe.
Workers and orchestrators must share a lock authority before concurrent worktree mutation.
Task and session registries must observe consistent transitions across instances.
Append order and replay determinism must be preserved with one append authority per log.
Tier and approval checks must remain fail-closed across scaled workers and MCP boundaries.
Per-instance pools must compose to a bounded total below database limits.

load_balancer_readiness.trace_propagation: required across load balancer and service hops
load_balancer_readiness.auth_header_preservation: required; authorization, Telegram, MCP, and operator ingress headers must not be stripped
load_balancer_readiness.rate_limit_behavior: required; rate limits must remain fair and fail-closed across instances

unsupported_scaling_modes.reason: External worker pools require separate activation, lock, registry, credential, and network evidence.
Multiple mutable registry-state writers/materializers can corrupt consistency.
Multiple Alembic migration runners can race schema changes.
Multiple clawhip appenders can duplicate or reorder event-log appends.
Dashboard/static remains future-ingress readiness only, not a live scalable service.
Runtime production audit emitters remain deferred and are not activated by scaling readiness.

rollback_and_observability.scale_down_fallback: required return path to single-host/local defaults and one-instance service counts
rollback_and_observability.version_skew: required detection for mixed image/schema/API versions before and during scale changes
rollback_and_observability.lag_backpressure: required metrics for event-log lag, queue/backpressure, and replay delay
rollback_and_observability.pool_saturation: required per-instance and aggregate DB pool saturation signals

validates: readiness-only mode and deferred production activation
scale-safety matrix for registry-api registry-state telegram-gateway orchestrator-adapter worker-wrapper and clawhip-daemon
singleton authorities for registry-state materializer Alembic migrations retention/apply/destructive lifecycle event append and clawhip bridge
coordination boundaries for idempotency shared storage worktree locks registry consistency event ordering capability tiers and bounded DB pools
load-balancer readiness for health/readiness trace propagation auth header preservation rate limits no host ports and no external load balancer
unsupported scaling modes for external worker pool multi-writer registry-state multi-runner migration multi-clawhip appenders dashboard live scaling and runtime audit emitter activation
rollback and observability requirements without credential rendering

non_goals: no production credentials or token values
